National Election Studies
National Election Studies
Lokniti-CSDS has a long and illustrious history of conducting National Election Studies during the Lok Sabha elections. Unbroken since 1996, this tradition has emerged as a veritable wealth of data regarding the political and social attitudes and choices of the Indian citizen around the election time. Most studies on Indian politics today would be incomplete without the wisdom and insight that these National Election Studies have provided. Academicians, journalists, scholars and the general public would all find this as an inexhaustible and treasured source of empirical details about the subject of politics in the country. Interested researchers are encouraged to browse through the attachments below. They can then call upon the Data Unit at Lokniti to get access to specifics that interest them.

State Election Studies
State Election Studies
Since 1995, Lokniti-CSDS has endeavored to study most of the Vidhan Sabha elections that take place in the country. Over the years, this database has grown tremendously to the point that we now have time-series data for all the states of India. Some of these election studies are in the form of Post Poll surveys, while some others are in the form of Pre Polls. In some other states researchers will find that multiple rounds of Trackers too were conducted before the actual election, mainly to ascertain the political shifts in the state. Together all these different instruments provide important insights into demographic details, political choices and social attitudes of the people around the time of elections.
Researchers can find the questionnaires for each of the surveys by following the links given below. Many of the questionnaires are in Hindi, so please ensure you have a Hindi font. Otherwise you can  download the font and copy it into your fonts folder. A detailed account of marginals (report) for many of the surveys can also be found here.

As per the provision of Article 79 of Indian Constitution, the House of the People, the Lok Sabha is the lower House of the parliament. Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of the adult suffrage. The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.

Parliament Functioning in Budget Session 2025
The Budget Session of Parliament was held between January 31 and April 4, 2025. Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha functioned for 26 days. This note looks at the functioning of both the Houses during this period.

The Winter Session of Parliament was held between November 25 and December 20, 2024.  Lok Sabha functioned for 20 days and Rajya Sabha for 19 days.  This note looks at the functioning of both the Houses during this period.

Parliament in Inaugural and Budget Session 2024
The 18th Lok Sabha held its first two sessions between June and August 2024. These two sessions lasted for a total of 22 days in Lok Sabha and 20 days in Rajya Sabha.  Both Houses adjourned a day ahead of schedule.

Profile of the 18th Lok Sabha
The results of the election to the 18th Lok Sabha were declared on 4th June, 2024.  Results have been declared for all 543 constituencies.  This note looks at the profile of the newly-elected members of the 18th Lok Sabha.
Read More

Profile of Candidates Contesting in General Elections 2024
Elections to the 18th Lok Sabha are being held between 19th April and 1st June, 2024. 8,360 candidates are contesting elections across 543 constituencies. This note looks at the profiles of candidates contesting these elections.
Read More

Functioning of the 17th Lok Sabha
The 17th Lok Sabha held its sessions between June 2019 and February 2024. In these five years, Lok Sabha functioned for 88% of its scheduled time, while Rajya Sabha worked for 73%. In September 2023, Parliament moved to a new building.
Read More
Download
Participation of MPs in the 17th Lok Sabha
This note looks at the participation of Lok Sabha MPs during the 17th Lok Sabha. MPs who are ministers, and the Speaker do not ask questions or introduce private member bills. Ministers represent the government during debates. On average, about 5%-7% of members of Lok Sabha act as Ministers at any point in time.
Read More

Women in Parliament and State Assemblies
The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on September 19, 2023.  The Bill seeks to reserve one-third of all seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.  A similar Bill had been introduced in Rajya Sabha in 2008, and was passed by the House two years later.  It lapsed after the dissolution of the 14th Lok Sabha in 2014.  This note takes a look at participation of women in Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.
Read More

70 years of Parliament
On May 13, 2022, Parliament completes 70 years since its first sitting.  The first session of the first Lok Sabha (LS) and Rajya Sabha (RS) commenced on May 13, 1952.  Currently, the 17th Lok Sabha (2019-2024) is ongoing.  In this note, we look at how the membership and functioning of the Parliament have changed since its first session.
